clue.text: Previous message in a bottle?

definitions.meaning: in British slang 'previous' is a criminal history, as in 'he has previous'
Message in a Bottle was a 1979 hit single by the band The ..., so it is one of their discs

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what the earlier note sealed in a bottle said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Previous' is British slang for a criminal past; the question mark flags the second reading, the song by The Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a list of past convictions, and a disc released by the band The Police.

clue.text: She opened a box of letters from Dad?

definitions.text: She opened a box of letters from Dad?

parts.words: She opened a box of letters from Dad?
parts.note: the mythical woman who opened the forbidden box, with a joke

explanation.surface: A woman opens a parcel of correspondence sent by her father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like correspondence, but it means the two letters of PA (Dad): P and/or A, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Pandora opened the jar or box that let the world's evils loose.

clue.text: Look, baby, that's not a pressure group!

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, as in 'lo and behold'

indicators.note: the clue says the word baby without a, so that letter is taken out of it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tells an infant that this is not a group that applies pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobby is an organised group campaigning to sway lawmakers, a pressure group.

clue.text: Man essentially fat — it's his bread

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: the essence of each of the words fat, it's and his is its central letter, so the middle of each is taken

explanation.surface: A fat man claims a loaf as his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' works on three words: the middle letters of fAt, iTs and hIs give A, T, I.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat unleavened Indian bread, so it is a kind of bread.

clue.text: See 1
They leave old tune out

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of tune are rearranged

explanation.surface: Musicians walk off rather than play a dated melody.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeunt is the Latin stage direction meaning that several characters go off stage.

clue.text: Not going out with macho types, you finally become available

indicators.note: going out read as departing from its usual form, so the letters of not are rearranged

parts.note: he-men are macho types

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of you

explanation.surface: Someone who stops dating muscle-bound men finds themselves free again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not going out' reads like staying in, but 'going out' is the anagram signal working on 'Not'; 'macho types' are he-men.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the menu is offered and can be had, so it is available.

clue.text: Degenerates rejecting holy books for many years

indicators.note: rejecting means turning away, so the holy books' letters are removed

parts.note: decadents are people in moral decline, degenerates
NT is the New Testament, a set of holy books

explanation.surface: Debauched people spurn scripture for a long stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A decade is ten years, so several decades are many years.

clue.text: Jump scared, being a youngster

parts.note: to spring is to jump
chicken means cowardly or scared

explanation.surface: A child leaps in fright.
explanation.definitionFit: 'No spring chicken' is said of someone no longer young, so a spring chicken is a young person.

clue.text: Representative of pretentious nobility

indicators.note: a representative sample is a small part of the whole, so a few letters inside the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A snooty person is held up as typical of a showy upper class.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across pretentiouS NOBility, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A snob looks down on others and apes the upper class, typical of pretentious aristocrats.

clue.text: First part of appeal by Romeo to seduce novice

indicators.note: the opening portion of the word appeal is taken, here its first three letters

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to entice is to tempt or seduce

explanation.surface: A charmer uses the opening of a plea to lure an innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First part of appeal' here gives APP, three letters rather than one.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice is a learner of a trade, a beginner or novice.

clue.text: Cold and shivering, crazy about love

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters go round the love
shivering means shaking, so the letters of crazy are jumbled

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone cold and trembling is mad about romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shivering' rearranges CRAZY; 'about' puts that round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Coryza is the medical term for a head cold, the inflamed nose of the common cold.

clue.text: Suggestion made by boozer on due process

parts.note: boozer is British slang for a pub, an inn

indicators.note: to process is to work over, so the letters of on due are reorganised

explanation.surface: A proposal comes from a pub about proper legal procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Due process' looks like the legal phrase, but 'process' rearranges ON DUE to UENDO.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an oblique hint, a sly suggestion.

clue.text: City came first before village in fiction

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of came is taken

parts.note: Ambridge is the fictional village in The Archers, a long-running BBC radio soap

explanation.surface: A city got going before a village in a novel did.
explanation.walkthrough: AMBRIDGE is the made-up village of The Archers, a BBC radio soap opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge is an English university city.

clue.text: Batman's plot, if convoluted, is the first in which to get immersed

definitions.text: the first in which to get immersed

indicators.note: convoluted means twisted and tangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tangled storyline for Batman is the first place to get stuck in.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby is baptised at a church's water basin, often a person's first ritual dipping.

clue.text: He or she with the Guardian who tormented 24

parts.note: ze is a gender-neutral pronoun used in place of he or she
a newspaper speaks of itself as we or us, and this is a Guardian puzzle

explanation.surface: Someone joins the newspaper in persecuting the person in 24.
explanation.walkthrough: ZE is a gender-neutral pronoun; the Guardian refers to itself as US.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the king of the gods punished the Titan who stole fire, chaining him to a rock.

clue.text: Bob kept locked up by 1 down

definitions.meaning: in the myth, the one thing left shut inside the box after the evils escaped was expectation of good things

explanation.definitionFit: Bob Hope the entertainer, and the optimism that stayed in the box in the Greek myth.

clue.text: Primarily hooked on gin, his work included

definitions.text: Primarily hooked on gin, his work included

indicators.note: the art is held within the run of opening letters
primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each of hooked, on, gin and his is taken

parts.note: art is creative work

explanation.surface: An artist hooked on gin put it into his work.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of Hooked On Gin His give HOGH; 'included' puts ART inside. The whole clue evokes his print Gin Lane, a picture of a gin-sodden London street.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hogarth's engraving Gin Lane shows the ruin gin brought to 18th-century London.

clue.text: Self-styled reference, lexicon, dictionary and so forth

definitions.text: Self-styled reference, lexicon, dictionary and so forth

parts.words: Self-styled reference, lexicon, dictionary and so forth
parts.note: the clue is styled as a list of near-synonyms, the way an entry in a book of synonyms reads, and that book is itself a reference work

explanation.definitionFit: A book listing words of similar meaning is laid out as runs of synonyms like the clue.

clue.text: Soft sea creature, tailless and timid

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter of the creature is dropped

parts.note: a squid is a sea creature
shy means timid

explanation.surface: A soft-bodied marine animal is described as lacking a tail and nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Squishy means yielding and squashable, soft to the touch.

clue.text: Strange uniform governess put conservative leader in

parts.note: Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: put signals placing the first letter of conservative into the nanny
in tells where the conservative leader goes: inside the nanny

parts.note: a nanny looks after children, as a governess does

indicators.note: leader means the front letter of conservative

explanation.surface: A uniformed nanny installed a Tory party leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncanny means weird and unsettling, strange.

clue.text: Figure is poorly situated after I'd gone

indicators.note: poorly means badly, so the letters are rearranged
after joins with gone: once the letters of I'd have left
gone means removed, so the I and D are taken out of situated

explanation.surface: A figure is badly placed once someone has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after I'd gone' takes I and D out of SITUATED, leaving STUATE; 'poorly' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a carved or cast figure.

clue.text: Selfish attempt to disrupt regenerated cities

indicators.note: to disrupt is to break into, so the attempt goes inside
regenerated means rebuilt, so the letters of cities are rearranged

parts.note: a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: A self-centred bid to upset urban renewal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regenerated' looks like part of the urban-renewal picture but is the anagram signal; 'to disrupt' means the attempt breaks into the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoistic means self-centred, putting one's own interests first.

clue.text: In June, Scotland is a cultural hub

indicators.note: in signals letters found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Scotland in summer is a centre for the arts, presumably the Edinburgh festivals.
explanation.definitionFit: The United Nations agency for education, science and culture is a cultural hub.

clue.text: Delicate female drowned in rising river

indicators.note: drowned in means submerged inside the river
rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the Nile is a river

explanation.surface: A frail woman drowned in a river that had risen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NILE into ELIN; 'drowned in' puts F inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means small and delicate, like an elf.

clue.text: One bound for America with Philistine on board

indicators.note: on board means inside, so the setter goes in

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
the US is America
Philistine is the setter, who calls themself me

explanation.surface: Someone heads to America with the setter on the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Philistine' is the setter, so ME. 'Bound' looks like headed for, but means chained, as in Aeschylus's play Prometheus Bound.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titan who stole fire was chained to a rock as punishment, the subject of Prometheus Bound.

clue.text: See 14
Key in her top type

indicators.note: in signals the key goes inside her

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A key sits in her best outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A halter top is a style of sleeveless top held by a strap round the neck.

clue.text: City couples, happily married, on the telly at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of each word from couples to telly

explanation.surface: City couples, contentedly wed, finally appear on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Sydney is the largest city in Australia.
